# Misp Tools

## Overview

gSage AI — MISP Analyze tool.

## Tools in this group

| Tool | Summary | Permissions | Requires approval | Core |
| --- | --- | --- | :---: | :---: |
| `misp_analyze` | MISP intelligence analysis: similarity, diff, explanation, tag suggestions, merge suggestions, report generation, graphs | `misp:read` | — | — |
| `misp_dashboard` | MISP managerial dashboards: overview, timeline, top tags, top galaxies, top orgs, threat level, distribution, feed health, sightings, attribute types, warninglists, ATT&CK matrix | `misp:read` | — | — |
| `misp_manage` | Create / update / delete MISP events, attributes, objects, tags, sightings and event reports | `misp:write` | ✓ | — |
| `misp_search` | Hybrid unified MISP search: events, attributes, IOCs, tags, galaxies. Use 'query' for automatic hybrid search; 'scope' for domain-specific queries. | `misp:read` | — | — |

## Configuration

> The JSON below goes into the **configtool model** in the web UI (per organisation; can also be scoped to a department).

> **Multiple profiles supported** — you may create more than one config row per organisation, each with a distinct `profile_id`. The agent picks one via the `config_profile` parameter at call time. State, rate limits and circuit-breaker counters are isolated per profile.

> **Sensitive fields** (api keys / passwords / tokens) are *omitted* from the JSON below — set them via environment variables (see the _Environment variables_ table) or directly in the encrypted DB row from the web UI.

### Empty configtool template (required fields only)

```json
{
  "url": "<value>",
  "api_key": "<value>"
}
```

### Example configtool model

```json
{
  "api_key": "<value>",
  "default_analysis": 0,
  "default_distribution": 0,
  "default_threat_level": 2,
  "url": "<value>",
  "verify_cert": true
}
```

### Field reference

| Field | Type | Required | Sensitive | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | :---: | :---: | --- | --- |
| `api_key` | `string` | ✓ | — | — | MISP API authentication key (AuthKey). |
| `default_analysis` | `integer` | — | — | `0` | Default analysis level: 0=Initial, 1=Ongoing, 2=Completed. |
| `default_distribution` | `integer` | — | — | `0` | Default distribution for new events: 0=YourOrg, 1=Community, 2=Connected, 3=All, 4=SharingGroup. |
| `default_threat_level` | `integer` | — | — | `2` | Default threat level: 1=High, 2=Medium, 3=Low, 4=Undefined. |
| `url` | `string` | ✓ | — | — | Base URL of the MISP instance (e.g. https://misp.example.com). |
| `verify_cert` | `boolean` | — | — | `true` | Verify TLS certificate (default: true). |

## Environment variables

The variables below are derived automatically from each tool's `config_schema`. Set them in your `.env` (or via your secrets backend) to seed defaults for every organisation. **Per-org DB config takes precedence over env vars.**

| Variable | Maps to field | Type | Default | Sensitive | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | :---: | --- |
| `TOOL_MISP__API_KEY` | `api_key` | `string` | — | — | MISP API authentication key (AuthKey). |
| `TOOL_MISP__DEFAULT_ANALYSIS` | `default_analysis` | `integer` | `0` | — | Default analysis level: 0=Initial, 1=Ongoing, 2=Completed. |
| `TOOL_MISP__DEFAULT_DISTRIBUTION` | `default_distribution` | `integer` | `0` | — | Default distribution for new events: 0=YourOrg, 1=Community, 2=Connected, 3=All, 4=SharingGroup. |
| `TOOL_MISP__DEFAULT_THREAT_LEVEL` | `default_threat_level` | `integer` | `2` | — | Default threat level: 1=High, 2=Medium, 3=Low, 4=Undefined. |
| `TOOL_MISP__URL` | `url` | `string` | — | — | Base URL of the MISP instance (e.g. https://misp.example.com). |
| `TOOL_MISP__VERIFY_CERT` | `verify_cert` | `boolean` | `true` | — | Verify TLS certificate (default: true). |
| `TOOL_MISP_MANAGE__AUTO_APPROVE` | `auto_approve` | `boolean` | `false` | — | When true, HITL approval requests for this tool are auto-approved by the backend without human review. Useful for lab/dev environments. DB toolconfig overrides env TOOL_<NAME>__AUTO_APPROVE; default is false. |

_Note: any field above can also be overridden per-tool by using the prefix `TOOL_<TOOL_NAME>__` instead of the shared `TOOL_<NAMESPACE>__` — useful when a single tool in the family needs a distinct value._
